note: Reviewer names omitted. Order is the Play page default, not by date. Not a complete set. In this sample 70 of 540 reviews are 1 or 2 stars (13%); the shown order is the page's default, so these counts are not the app's overall rating.

reviews.text: The app was never great, but it served its purpose. Since the recent update (June 2024) I can no longer log in at all. If I click on the Facebook option to log in, I immediately get an error message without even being able to enter any information. The error I get is "Your Facebook email is unavailable. Contact customer care to resolve." I'm a co-author on a site for my dad while he battles pancreatic cancer, and the last thing I need is login issues on a stupid app.

Provides an easy way to communicate updates on a recovering person's status without having to be constantly updating people individually. It does ask for donations whenever you visit, but I have not donated and I am still able to access it. It is sometimes a little difficult to access the journal entries. I get a notice there is a new journal entry but in the app instead of going to that entry it goes to a list of dates and notifications of journal entries, but eventually there.

The app is helpful for posting quick updates but the missing features and problems listed by others are all still there. I have to go to the website to see who liked a post and visitor info. I can't read the comments. Photos show as included when I hit Post but they are only in the Gallery and not part of the post. Captioning is also glitchy.

this app simply doesn't work. I can log in on mobile web but the app fails and I can't get into it. On mobile web trying to make a post is impossible as every keystroke send the cursor to the beginning of the textarea and duplicates the entire word as it's typed. this may not be the worst app I've used but it's certainly not a good one for a mobile device.

I hate to say it because I think CaringBridge is a fantastic website and it's been invaluable to us during my husband's cancer treatment. But this app is honestly pretty bad. Clicking any external link (and some internal links) crashes the app completely. You cannot see who hearts a post from the app. Navigating the site settings is unintuitive. Posting journal entries is super easy though. If you just need to fire off quick updates, then the app will work well for you.

This has been so convenient for my family, thanks!! I recommend it! Better than repeating details to everyone individually. Sign up was easy and no worries about which social media platform everyone is on. The app is a little buggy with lists, e.g., duplicate entries (that don't exist on web). But overall it functions well and does everything we need it to.

When I was first invited to join the Caring Bridge, it waa via email. I had no idea there was an app. I received my emails but i had to sift through different emails. When another friend created a profile for Carimg Bridge I was following two people. I learned of the app and it made it much easier to track the stories and pictures posted and to read comments. The app is the best way to keep in touch!! I just log in and see if there are new stories, and much easier than sifting through email.

Nice app but does have some glitches. Sometimes uploading photos works and sometimes it doesn't. Also had trouble with adding a link for a related article into my latest post. I was able to finally add photos and the article link through editing the post on the website rather than through the app. Lastly, on both the app and website it seems that I can only re-read my posts from the last six months or so, but not before. It seems to get stuck retrieving the older ones.

I like the convenience of checking Caring Bridge through the app and even just writing text updates. However, this app fails when it comes to adding photos. There is no way for me to add a photo through the app. I even had planned ahead and added photos from my desktop computer and saved it as a draft. Then I wrote the text for the post from the app and posted it. The photos disappeared when I posted it! Very disappointing and frustrating!

I love the intention of the app, but its so buggy and glitchy that I just use the website instead. Less hassle. If they can get the bugs worked out I may go back, but they're in serious need of an update. Glitches: can't attach photos, can't edit posts, can't save drafts, the spinning circle just spins and spins and spins and never progresses past "loading."

In general, I like it, but definitely some major differences between using the app and going online. Doesn't show everything in the app. Currently pictures are causing the app to force close, and it would be spectacular if you could comment on the Well Wishes that were sent. Makes writing a journal entry necessary if you want to be able to respond to people. The app is okay in a pinch, but still could use some work.

Great tool. I've used Caring Bridge several times over the years. It's been wonderful at saving time keeping friends and family informed so I could commit more time supporting my family member who is sick. The app is a handy extension of the website. However, both the app and the website are due for updates. The interfaces are clunky and awkward by modern standards. Why can't I see all the journal entries in one list? Why is it so difficult to figure out how to get back to journal entries from?

I love what the app does, but it's kind of buggy. I'm on android 8.0 and tapping the notifications would not take me to the journal entry. This seems to be working, now. However, selecting older journal entries only takes me to the most current entry. To get to an older journal entry you have to tap next until you get to the desired entry.

The actual website is so much better. the app didn't give me any notifications of new journal entries. It also had the incorrect time stamp on journal entries - forexample something that was posted in the morning wouldn't post on the app until the following day but when I went to the website it showed up right away. That's a very significant lag. It would also show that 3 different journal entries were posted at the exact same time when in reality they were hours apart.

I have only been using the CaringBridge platform and app for about 24-36 hours, but it has already streamlined my communications with tons of family and friends while my parents are both in the hospital. I really appreciate the overall ease of use and simple integration with Facebook, which enabled me to reach even more people. There are a few minor glitches with the app but I was able to adjust a few things on my laptop when I had a chance, so the glitches didn't significantly derail me.

I really like caring bridge when I access it on my computer- it's a phenomenal way to keep family/friends updated. But this phone app leaves so much to be desired. It is not easy to navigate. I'm having trouble downloading photos . It frequently gives me the "circle of thinking/ indecision". I don't need the extra stress of dealing with a faulty app when I'm dealing with a critically ill family member.

More limited than I had hoped. Doesn't allow me to post photos or responses to comments. No way to approve visitor access requests. I wanted a way to post from my long chemo sessions or when I was out. I still need to get on my PC when I get home and edit everything and often I'm too exhausted after treatment to do the extra step. Defeats the purpose of having an app. For the sake of the patient, improve the functionality! Looks like reviews have been complaining about this for a while.

While great in concept, the execution of this app is clunky and hard to use. The button to approve visitors is hidden in settings icon. It would be easier if it had a dedicated button on the main page. Also photos I upload on app keep disappearing. Uploading photos on website is no prob. Be careful with donations. It gives you an error message after you enter cc info making you think it didn't go through. It goes through alright and hits your cc activity right away. Uninstalling! Go to website

This is a great app to stay informed when you have a loved one with a medical issue. As a family member you can post to keep a wide group up to date and not have to make individual calls, emails or texts. It is easy to use, make comments on posts, etc. People can sign up to get notifications or just check the app for new posts.

CaringBridge is aptly named giving those with major medical challenges a way to connect first person with those outside the situation. The app provides most of the features found on the web version amd is extremely user friendly. I have personally journaled for three family members and followed several others. The app provides users with immediate notifications of updates. Highly recommend.

Web version on my phone is much better than the app. App doesn't consistently display photos in journal entries (they appear briefly then disappear, but tapping the blank space opens the hidden photo). So doesn't show previews of YouTube links. The app counts comments differently than the web version (app doesn't count replies). Probably more shortcomings but this is enough for me to uninstall.

The app is very buggy and doesn't open sometimes. Certain elements of the page do not work when viewed on the app. For example, you cannot see who liked a journal entry through the app but you can if you use the website version. Photos also appear blurry at times. Journal entry date and time stamps are also inaccurate.

Deleted my previous 5 star after I started using the app. The reason for the new rating is because of this: I have frequent problems using the qwerty keyboard and so I like to be able to see what I am typing. When I try to type on the app, it adds space under what I have typed to put the text out of view. I find I have to frequently adjust and sometimes it glitches and adds a bunch of new lines, and won't stop. It may be a lag issue now that I think about it but that alone could be app breaking
excellent service for friends and families!

Bad app. Just hosts the website. Doesn't keep you logged in or give notifs. I found myself getting updates on email, then trying to see them in the app, having to log back in each time, then dig for the update because sorting by new doesn't work. Don't waste your time, just use Chrome.

Some functions don't work. I cannot see who reacted with a heart on journal entries, only the number of hearts. Also cannot read comments, tapping on the link does nothing. Some visitors are prompted to create an account every time they open it. I HATE that the author is included in number of visits and you can't customize. Why would anyone want to count how many times they visit their own page? I contacted the developer who said "we'll consider your suggestion".

I love it because I don't have to keep calling her to find out how she's doing. It notifys me when she writes in her journal and I can check it when I notice it. I don't miss a call if that work. It allows her to rest without receiving many phone calls or text messages. She makes one post everyone who signed in on her journal will receive a notification.

This app is terrible. I couldn't find any link to the mobile app on the website. So, I signed up on the webpage to get email notifications for updates. That's not ideal. I found the app later and was able to log in with the email I used to create my account. Now I have two accounts, one created with Google and one not. To make matters worse, the mobile app can't find the person I'm looking for. You should be ashamed of yourselves.

Although the app was functional early on in my use as an Author for a family member, the mobile app has become progressively worse after use over a few weeks. I am unable to add any photos or write a journal without issues with the cursor moving downward on the page on its own. I've already uninstalled/re-installed the app without any positive results. Please resolve issues so we can properly use the mobile app as you promote it to be for sharing health updates with family and friends.

The new changes are terrible!!! Horrible layout, no gallery tab, so you have to scroll through all posts to find pictures. You have really downgraded the app and website!! We have lost half our followers, as they can no longer login or navigate through the site. The story used to be collapsed, now you have to scroll through the whole thing to see the latest posts. It feels like the website and app are straight out of the 90's.

Ths app has been a God-send during my dad's month long journey through emergency back surgery and subsequent complications. I just sent one email with the Caring Bridge link to everyone who might be interested in following his progress. They can choose for themselves whether or not to receive all of the updates, and I only have to send one post when it's time to update. Also, There are two of us posting to the site so we can avoid sending duplicate updates.

I don't usually do reviews, however, this is a wonderful app!! It allows you get updated information on how your loved one is doing without sending a lot of messages to the family during such difficult times. It updates immediately as the family posts an entry. It also allows you to send well wishes & comments.

I like this app for ease of use and because visitors can get information without having to sign up. I do wish the meal train was included on this site rather than a third-party site. As a caregiver, that would make coordinating all aspects of care easier. I have used other care sites that include this feature. With that said, I deeply appreciate this site and all that it allows me to do!

The CaringBridge app. is a great way to let people know about a loved ones continuous progress during an illness, treatment, rehabilitation, or recovery. The app. allows you to send post to your friends and family to keep them up to date on someone's care. The app. is so easy to use and very user friendly. I have used the app. to follow my friend's treatment through their illness and stay informed about what was happening.

It's just ok. I should have done a Facebook page instead. On CaringBridge you can only upload 3 photos at a time. The photos are always blurry. It doesn't let you post videos. Things glitch all the time in the app. It is super frustrating. It gets the job done but not the best.

My experience with the app has vastly improved even over the past year. Photos are uploading more quickly. Captions are easier to add via the app, and the overall experience as an author has gone much smoother. The CaringBridge option provides such a respectful, private, and appropriately sober platform for families and friends experiencing distressful situations.

The website a great platform for keeping folks up to date, but the app is terrible. Journal updates done on the website don't show up on the app. It crashes, and is very glitchy, photos disappear, and you can't "like/heart" people's comments on the app, just on the website. Use the website, don't bother annoying yourself with this app...it's terrible.

When someone is seriously ill there are many friends and family who want to check on how it is going. It can be overwhelming responding and you are never sure who you told what to. Caring Bridge brings some sanity and a measure of consistency to that. It doesn't eliminate the need to provide more info to some but it certainly greatly reduces one of the stress point of a major illness. It is so appreciated I would recommend this to any who are feeling overwhelmed with calls and notes to update

I had initial problems setting up my account, but now that I have completed that, I find the site to be a great way to track the situation of someone I care about without being intrusive. Being able to offer supportive notes is great.
1 person found this review helpful

Using the app is good. Getting out of it? Not so much. Everytime I read a friend's entry and try to exit or close the app, everything locks up but a little processing spinner. I end up having to restart my phone to return to normal. I deleted the app.

The concept and intention is amazing. It has really helped me keep people informed. It is VERY buggy though. When you don't feel well it is frustrating to write out a whole post and have it refuse to go through or look like it hasn't posted but then posts 5 times. I can't see who has hearted anything, which totally sucks. Apparently my loved ones are having issues on their end too. Do not like the donation requests. I would rather have just paid it myself and have my people left alone.

Does this only work with the old CaringBridge, or something? I'm new to the site, created an account, and notice all this lack of functionality and the FAQs are for the old site. I can't even use my login credentials to sign into the app, and I was pretty sure I didn't forget my password. Nevertheless, did the "forgot my password link" and it won't email me a reset link. Something is not working properly.

I would of given it a 5 star but I had an tech issue with the email I provided; it was resolved after 2 hours & not my fault. It would be cool if you could make your own get well/condolence stamp/card. Type whatever you want w/a image preselected image from caring bridge inventory.

I will try this again. It says new and improved. We will see. I LOVE Caring Bridge. My daughter and I are both authors on her sons page. we use the website as the app has had a lot of issues....not seeing who hearts a post, not seeing replies or comments on posts, not being able to add pictures... the list goes on. If this time around goes better, then I will update my review. *** As an author, it doesn't work like the website. I uninstalled again.

App is completely non functional for me. Google Auth gets sent to mobile web and fails to return the sign-in to the application. I'm logged in, but in the mobile web version instead of the application. Requesting one-time sign in emails also never sends an email. I have tried several times over the past year.

I open the CaringBridge app, click on my journal, click the "Allow" button, and the app crashes. (I'm on a Galaxy S20 which popped up a message saying the app crashed because there's a bug in it.) I'm reverting to posting journals, etc. via the website.

Very user friendly for both author and readers. I started using it 5 yrs ago for my wife who has ongoing problems with brain issues. After not using it for 3 years she had a relapse I was able to restart it with no problems and my readers received notification of my new post immediately.

Pixel 3 phone. I follow a couple people on CB, and when I select one to read their entries, the app hangs, to the point of not responding to the phone's Back arrow, so I have to manually kill the app. CB's mobile web site works just fine for me, so I'm uninstalling the app.

Great for posting to everyone, so you don't have to respond to each well meaning person's inquires about how you feel, what's going on, etc. If the readers sign up they'll get notified each time there is a post, so they won't miss anything, and can leave comments. Love it!

I am thankful for this tool. The site has a few glitches loading seemlessly from the email notices of site activity to the actual site without error messages. I was used to functionality in Facebook and gmail with back button etc which can be a bit fussier on this site. Once I got used to navigating Caring Bridge, I knew how to get around these issues. These glitches could be solved by a programmer. Overall, Caring Bridges offers a great service and is well done.

CaringBridge provides a useful platform for caregivers and family to share updates regarding a loved one who is experiencing an ongoing troublesome issue to friends and family who care about them. For those posting updates, the app is a less polished experience compared to the website: photos disappear from drafts, submitting a post doesn't always actually submit the post, and other issues I've experienced, so I hope the dev team can give those aspects some care and attention.

The app was ok until they started pushing several notifications a week asking for donations. I want notifications turned on so I know when my family member posts but now I consistently get notifications about other nonsense. Encourage your loved ones to find another platform to share on, this is utter garbage. There is no way to customize what types of notifications you get.

We have used this service a couple of times now for critical medical events. Family and friends have told us MANY times how much they value the ability to get updates regularly. It's easy to manage and use, limiting access to those we approve, and has been so valuable in limiting the time we spend on requests for info so that we can focus on our loved one. I highly recommend this service/app and am deeply grateful for it!

I have used this app for myself and for several friends now. It is so helpful. It provides a means for giving updates to friends and family just once and not having to repeat yourself over and over, which can be exhausting. And it allows those friends and family to keep up to date and to provide encouragement. Highly recommend.

This app is an amazing way to keep family and friends updated when a loved one is going through an illness or any medical condition. It is an amazing resource to update in real time and eliminate miscommunication. It has several other features such as a calendar for others to use to help support loved one and their family and options for linking in meal train and go fund me links. Truly 10stars!

On most of the various platforms I've been juggling, its JUST THE BEST (some older tablets make me sign in new every time or get hung up). When a dear one is going through a true scare there's no time to be further scattered answering individual 'how are they's [tho the askers won't maybe see this] I just keep pointing anyone with web access to this, and am maybe feeling a bit of a release in authoring these updates (also in inviting other loving care-ers to take a turn) .
1 person found this review helpful

Other than the fact that people could technically use Facebook to update friends and family for free... and a little pressure to donate to this organization all over it, also you have to download yet another app into your phone, I'm glad I got to stay in the loop with my friends healing journey. It's easy to use!

Great app to inform freinds n family. Means when I'm poorly, I only have to write one update, and everyone gets it. People can dip in as and when they like. Preferred this to more mainstream FB, because I wanted to keep it simple for lots of older family who don't do social media. Dropped a star, just because it asks for donations. I understand why, but we all want everything for nothing, don't we :) . Does what I need so happy.
1 person found this review helpful

Very easy to log in and get notifications for the blogs you follow. The app allows for a much more seamless process to read and comment on a new post when I'm on my phone rather than attempting to navigate the mobile website.
App crashes frequently. Many of the links are not working. When you select the link, the app crashes right away. Access via computer is better but I wish it worked on my phone.

This is an amazing app to keep informed about loved ones who are in the hospital. I have 2 ones, 1 on each side of the family, that I get updates. No annoying group texts. Even family members in Europe can keep up to date. I wish I had known about this when my parents were in the hospital. Keeping family and friends updated through calls and texts was a constant concern. This app gives the family there with the patient the ability to post and read replies at their convenience.

I love this app. I needed to use it 10 years ago and find myself needing it again. The only thing I find a little difficult is finding where to make your journal entry. Then when you save it as a draft it's not obvious where to find it.

I recommend this app to anyone who is dealing with trying to keep family and friends informed while dealing with even more important issues with your health or whatever. It's super easy to use and they're larger community of friends love getting updates.

This was a useful.app for me. My only complaint was how each user got asked for money every time and it was represented as being to honor the recipient. I did not even know about it until someone told me. I think it should be reworded to sound less like it came from the user (myself,). Like."we are free to the user and need donations to keep it that way. We appreciate any donation you can make that will be posted as in honor of..."

I gave a rating of 4 stars, only because I feel the planner should be more prominent in the options and labeled clearly. It is placed lower in the selections but i feel it would be more user friendly for those that visit the site and want to help but are not as tech-savvy as the web designers.

This is a fantastic app to help those who are going through a health challenge and their families keep in touch with others by simply making updates to one website/blog, rather than posting on several social media websites and creating email lists, etc. Calendar tools also help when coordinating meals and other helps for the family. Highly recommend.

Do not like the latest update about a week plus ago. Can't turn it to landscape picture, the emoji's are gone, and adding pictures to a journal post doesn't work. Wish I could revert to the old version.

Caring Bridge has been a huge help with keeping family and friends updated without the stress of having to tell everyone individually. The app makes it convenient to provide quick updates and is super easy to use!

As author, I'm having a bit of trouble navigating the requests list. I can't seem to find it but I accidently get to it....would like a tab for authorizing requests. If it's there and I've missed it all day, I apologize.
1 person found this review helpful

I have used this app so many times and have found it to be the biggest blessing during times of such great need and encouragement and prayer. It was a lifeline straight from the heart of friends and loved ones exactly when we needed it. This makes the hardship and trials we all go thru easier, as we are not alone and many help carry us thru it! Thank you Caringbridge!

It could use improvements such as the ability to upload photos in Comments. I think Caring Bridge is asking too much $30 for a donation to help keep the website going. I run a website and it doesn't cost as much as they're asking. They would do better asking for $2 Patreon donations because they would probably get more people participating in donating. I don't like running into their big donation beg every time I read a journal entry

Absolutely love this app. It allows the ones going through something to update their loved ones on one place. It had so many features to help out those in need. It allows me to keep up with my loved ones when I cany physically be there for them.

Easy to use for myself to post updates and pictures and for my followers to read updates and make comments. Very nice for older people who arent on facebook to be able to get updates about their friends. Also easy to share on facbook. Saves time and keeps everyone informed.
A lot of features don't work right. The app won't allow me to add picture to my journal entries, and will only upload a few of the photos I'm trying to upload to the photo album.
This app freezes up on me almost every time I try to use it. I have to force stop and reopen to get it to work properly. I have tried deleting and reinstalling and it still does not fix the problem.

I am so glad to be able to keep up-to-date on a friend's journey through Leukemia, I enjoy the photos she shares, the update journals, and the ability to comment and interact with out disrupting her schedule. Great app for my phone!

This is a great app for keeping family and friends informed when faced with a medical condition. I know we are loved, cared for, and people want to be supportive. Rather than sending dozens of messages, one journal entry reaches our circle at the same time.
1 person found this review helpful

What an absolutely incredible app. It is so hard to text or communicate to so many concerned family and friends as we too endure tragedy and heart ache. But this gives a platform for encouragement and ease of communication that dwarfs anything out there, and provides a more private and intimate setting, as opposed to social media. Thank you to the amazing staff at the customer service for helping us when we had some issues during login and for the creators of this app. What a blessing it is.

Slow to update. I get email notifications that new journal entries and comments have been made but the app doesn't show the new entries until way later therefore I have to check the website to get the latest entries.
1 person found this review helpful

This app has been unbelievably supportive in my health journey! Being able to send friends and family the link when they ask how I'm doing, or before they come to visit and asking them to read it over instead of having to explain the same details over and over is more supportive than I could have believed. I am very impressed with the ability to post, comment, and I love that it's connected to GoFundMe and meal train apps as well! Thank you CaringBridge friends!!!

Made updating family and friends about my cancer journey easy, at a time that was already stressful. It is wonderful to be able to write one update and have it available to all my friends and loved ones. Would highly recommend to anyone dealing with a health issue, or dealing with a loved one's health issue. A simple tool for communication.

I have been using CaringBridge since 2011 after someone recommended it to me to share my health journey. I was telling her how I had so many people to update and she told me how easy it was with CaringBridge. That another friend of hers had used it so I should try it. We could have been a late night commercial. LOL It has helped me through several health events but mostly allowed me to keep those concerned about me up-to-date even after the initial incidents were over. App helps when not at PC.

Its such a good way to stay updated on what's happening in their life. The layout is easy to understand and I like that you're able to personalize your account. I imagine its also a very nice spot for them to share the good or bad news in one place versus having to share it through text over and over. All in all great app!

Absolutely LOVE this sight! Easy to enter. Not a bunch of ads popping up while you're trying to read. Extremely Easy to navigate from one person to another, if needed.
1 person found this review helpful

CaringBridge app is super easy to setup and provide updates to large groups of people! However the use of other capabilities like ways to help thru the planning page isn't as intuitive ... also I found the ads annoying.

Everything going well. Only problem I ran into was difficulty adding a few friends to the invite page. Tried several times so I wonder if others never got their invitations.
1 person found this review helpful
This app offers a chance to keep up with a loved one's process. It's not always easy to get around, sometimes requires logging out & returning to make a comment.

App just crashes at login. Message pops up that says app has a bug. I see there was a recent update, which must be the culprit. Edit: Thanks for the update. It does seem to be working fine now. Updated my review

Why do you keep screwing around with this site!? Now when I log in it shows me pages "I visit' from 10 years ago that I DONT WANT TO SEE!!! I deleted these pages off my account years ago yet there you are putting them right back into my account WITH NO OPTION to remove them! I have no choice but to delete this app now. You need to fire the people that tell you they are making this app better; they are and have ruined it. What a shame

This app was invaluable in giving me a sense of control during an period that was far from controllable. I am 6 years post cancer diagnosis and I still go back and read my posts and updates. To remind me of the journey beyond the physical scars. It is amazing what our minds protect us from.

I really like the CaringBridge app. I wish they had it for chromebook, too. My draft journals started on my android phone, do not show on my Chrome book. I haven't checked if the draft is saved on Chrome Book if it will show on phone.

On occasions, a post won't load, but I come back later and try again and all is functional. I haven't been successful in uploading photos but it may be because most of my posts are done via cell phone.

A great way to keep up with loved ones that may be going through some tough times. The most gratifying thing I have found with this app is keeping up with communication on how someone is doing without the bother of them having to answer a phone or text

I love this App. It keeps family and friends updated on information and relieves stress from the spouse/family so they don't have to keep up with everyone individually. I wish this existed when my husband had his stroke. It would have made my life so much simpler. Thank you for creating this App.💞

As a Stage IV colon cancer patient it has been an therapeutic outlet for us and our family and friends. We decided not to engage on Social Media about this as people do not have good sensitivity there. We have coordinated meal deliveries through the app and kept regular updates to my positive progress. Do not just use this app for terminaly ill but use it to educate the living. Great app snd highly recommended.

I have used caringbridge to follow several friends and family members' situations. It has helped us keep informed, connected and I cannot say enough good things about being able to share info without compromising health and also being able to provide love and comfort to your loved one's as they go through tough times.
1 person found this review helpful

The app is easy to use and easy to navigate. I started a caringbridge when my daughter was diagnosed with cancer. It has been a great way to keep friends and family informed without having to repeat ourselves a million times. The only thing with the app that I don't love is the donate button being front and center. The website is free to use and donations do not go to the families.
After the latest update, the app always crashes when attempting to open a journal entry. Also, many of the settings require opening the site in the browser, which defeats the purpose of the app.

DATA MINING APP? My account was deleted without warning or explanation after a month of use. The email I sent to customer support came back as invalid, making me think this app is just out there to steal your information.

Caring Bridge is our Go-To app when we have a medical situation. We are the parents of seven adult children and each have four siblings, plus we have many friends who want to be kept in the loop. CB makes it so much easier for us to keep everyone up to date. Thank you from the bottom of our hearts!!!!!
1 person found this review helpful

Frustrating app. You can't tell it to stop sending you email without it completely unfollowing. Why will you just not accept that the only way I want to be contacted of another post is by push notification?!
1 person found this review helpful

This site was developed for me when i was hospitalized. A good friend of mine posted updates on my progress so i could concentrate on healing.
